question: P, Q and R together can do a piece of work in 56 days. P and Q together can do one-fourth as much work as R alone. In how many days can P and Q together complete the entire work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

The efficiency of R = efficiency of (P + Q) × 4

Ratio of efficiencies of R : (P + Q) = 4 : 1

Total efficiency of P, Q, and R = 4 + 1 = 5

As they can finish the work in 56 days

⇒ Total work = 56 × 5 = 280

P and Q take time = 280/1 = 280

 ∴ The correct answer is 280 days

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: 

P, Q, and R together can do a piece of work in 56 days. 

P and Q together can do one-fourth as much work as R alone.

Concept used:

Total work = Work done per day × Total time taken

Calculation:

Let the efficiencies be P, Q, and R of the respective worker.

According to the question,

(P + Q) = R/4

⇒ 4(P + Q) = R ....(1)

So, the total work

⇒ (P + Q + R) × 56 = 56(P + Q + R) units

Now, P and Q together complete the entire work in

⇒ 56(P + Q + R)/(P + Q)

⇒ 56(P + Q)/(P + Q) + 56R/(P + Q)

⇒ 56 + (56 × 4(P + Q))/(P + Q)

⇒ 56 + (56 × 4)

⇒ 280

**∴ P and Q together complete the entire work in 280 days.**
